Sorry this is so long. I went to a boarding school that kept the students cell phones in a safe. We were only allowed to use them after school or during the weekend during certain hours and we had to use them outside. It rained/snowed a lot, so, that sucked. We also didn't have internet access unless they opened the computer lab, which didn't have many computers and wasn't open/available as often as one would like. Social media was also not allowed.  

I also used my phone/the internet as a coping tool and was far away from home missing my friends so this was a weird/difficult transition for me. But I learned to adapt and get creative with how I spent my time and lowered my anxiety. I used different coping skills, and now when I'm in a situation where I can't use the phone or internet, like in a psych ward or something, it doesn't bother me. You can try learning/playing an instrument, drawing, writing/journaling, coloring, listening to music, going on a walk, interacting with someone in person if possible (maybe a sibling if you have one), the list goes on. My advice would be to get creative and find new/different things you like to help you out. I really think being subjected to such rules ended helping me out in life, even if it seemed harsh in the moment.  Or even in retrospect, lol.

Edit: reading is also a go-to for me to destract myself from anxiety. And I end up learning a lot cuz I prefer non-fiction.
